posts.text: A major question in conservation science is whether species will be able to adapt to climate change by evolving. In the case of black-browed albatrosses, a model predicts that such evolutionary rescue is only likely in a low-emissions scenario. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/4KyE50ZRuxN

🗣️OECMs in Practice: Ecology, Implementation, and Monitoring

Sophie Elliot and Thomas Pienkowski will discuss different experiences in identifying, developing, and evaluating OECMs across marine and terrestrial ecosystems.

🗣️ Seeing Further: Innovations in Camera Trap Ecology 

 Organised by Fabiola Innarilli and Chris Sutherland, the session will explore emerging tools, their opportunities and limitations for effective ecological monitoring.

🗣️Beyond Forests

Kimberley Simpson, Jon Millett, Jess Rickenback & Elizabeth Telford will address escalating threats to open ecosystems and opportunities for resilience building and the need to prioritise it in the global environmental agenda.

🗣️ Bridging ecosystems across space

Organised by Alain Danet and Isamel Lajaaiti, the talk will explore how new developments such as food-web models, meta-ecosystem theory, and biodiversity data to understand ecosystems push ecology toward a more integrative, spatially explicit science.

Thematic sessions are a core part of the BES Annual Meeting, providing a space to explore critical questions facing ecology today. 

This year’s programme features exciting talks and discussions on ecological research and practice. Scroll to learn more 👇
